related_resources.reason: Chronology lists composition started 8 January 1926, British publication 5 May 1927, and 1928 Prix Femina. Preview is a partial book, not complete analysis.

Lists 1927 Hogarth Press publication; describes literary perspectives, gender and the intellectual freedom of self-publishing. Exhibition summary is not a proof of Woolf’s personal intention in each passage.

Records Talland House holidays in St Ives and the novel’s relocated Isle of Skye setting; biographical family history and death of Julia Stephen in 1895. Biographical source, not proof of fictional identity.
Catalogs corrections in Woolf’s handwriting on 1927 page proofs; documents her roles as writer, editor and publisher. Specific American editorial interventions must be checked against proofs.

Comparison of 1927 US/UK editions, the 1930 revised British impression, proof and section-number variants. Some editorial prescriptions are Mendelson’s judgments; do not flatten contested textual judgments into consensus.
Institutional summary of Woolf’s role in modernist fiction and Bloomsbury; a general assessment, not evidence of direct influence on specific later novelists.

historical_claims.anchor: Virginia Woolf published To the Lighthouse in nineteen twenty-seven.
Woolf remembered childhood holidays in St Ives, Cornwall
Woolf began serious work on the novel in nineteen twenty-six.
The British and American editions appeared in the same year, but their texts do not represent one mechanically identical state.
The Hogarth Press matters beyond a decorative imprint on the title page.
